tasks.title: level_pits fills wall-side voids next to footprints (S-019 / #155 live fail)
tasks.notes: Follow-up to #155. LIVE FAIL 2026-10-27: ground --apply on 48,-44 under site_lock planned 35 other pits then readback mismatches; seq 211 rolled back via site_recover. Tops at x 6145–6147, z -5520 stay y=36 vs neighbour (6144,-5520) y=44. Cause: (6146,-5520)/(6147,-5520) skipped by adj-to-footprint guard in level_pits; (6145,-5520) in a candidate component with bbox narrow=6 > PIT_MAX_WIDTH 5. Deliver: retune level_pits so free columns beside a footprint can fill to the outside rim (never raise footprint columns; never use footprint tops as the rim target). Raise PIT_MAX_WIDTH if the live 3-wide band's bbox needs it. Unit test: wall-side pit adjacent to fp fills to rim y; footprint columns unchanged; wide depression still skipped. Acceptance: ground rerun on 48,-44 under site_lock --world southampton-build; those three columns match y=44; no bad fill into footprints. Files: lib/layers/ground_layer.py, lib/layers/test_ground_layer.py. Helps: S-019 / I-015 void-beside-walls. Done 2026-10-27: removed adj-to-footprint candidate skip; PIT_MAX_WIDTH 5→6; wall-side pit unit test. Merged task/160-wall-side-pit-fill (b89aea4 / merge eba0213). Live ground rerun on 48,-44 still required for S-019 acceptance. LIVE RETUNE 2026-10-27: after adj-fp removal, wall-side band merges into candidate component bbox narrow=7 > PIT_MAX_WIDTH 6 (x 6144–6150); pits_filled 45 elsewhere but 6145–6147 stayed y=36; apply seq 213 rolled back (2 mismatches). Raising PIT_MAX_WIDTH and re-verifying. REVIEW 2026-10-27: state why the retune value is 7 and not a general rule (width of the live wall-side band vs PIT_MAX_WIDTH); say whether I-017 door floors (susu 42-A/B/C/D pit then ground 3-8 higher) and Jubilee panes below ground (I-013) clear once these columns fill, since door floors read the ground just outside each door. WAVE 2026-10-27: code on main (adj-fp removed, PIT_MAX_RADIUS Chebyshev gate); orchestrator live-verifying S-019 columns, not filing a duplicate ticket yet.

tasks.title: Feature doors clear the inward vestibule cell so door_to_wall is 0
tasks.notes: LIVE FAIL after #146 (2026-10-27): facade_plan on jubilee_w93729745 / susu_w33830305 / west_w34391673 / retail_w33830236; susu/jubilee/retail re-applied still show 11 door_to_wall lower-half flags (susu 6, west 3, jubilee 2; retail 0). Doubles short: west 40-A/40-B, susu 42-C, retail 57-A plan 2-leaf but land 1-leaf ('no pair cell'). Cause: feature_build._set_door_leaf clears the outside stoop only — never the inward cell (opposite DIRS[face]), so the storey floor / solid behind the door keeps door_to_wall. Do not invent facade_plan or floor_offset hacks — fix the door clear tool. Deliver: _set_door_leaf (or its caller) clears the inward column at door height the same way as the outside stoop (air through the door opening; leave floor underfoot); unit test that a door with solid inward at b+1/b+2 is cleared and floaters.door_to_wall does not fire; re-apply affected features under site_lock --world southampton-build; west_w34391673 still mismatched (seq 196) — fix/re-apply as part of acceptance. Acceptance: site_patrol (or floaters) shows 0 door_to_wall on those four features; planned double leaves land as 2-leaf where the wall has a pair cell. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_feature_build.py. Prior notes about #146 absorbing this were wrong — #146 removed the old portal path but left the stoop-only clear. REVIEW 2026-10-27: (1) Two-leaf landing is a separate limit: most 'no pair cell' fallbacks (west 40-A/40-B, susu 42-C, retail 57-A) have no second wall cell with a jamb either side on a rotated stepped wall, so this task will not turn them into 2-leaf; acceptance for #143 is 0 door_to_wall only, and two-leaf landing is carried by #164. (2) The vestibule fix leaves the storey floor underfoot. WAVE 2026-10-27: code already on main (inward clear + keep/lintel/plan/journal); orchestrator live-verifying acceptance, not re-implementing.

tasks.title: Trees layer reads mapped tree points and tree rows from the vector map
tasks.notes: Cause: OSMGround collects natural=tree points into .trees but no layer reads them; trees_layer takes lidar canopy plus the hand-read crown files only. natural=tree_row lines are not read at all. Deliver: use mapped tree points and tree rows as candidate crown positions in trees_layer (snap to lidar canopy peaks as #129 does; log each rejected point with its reason); tree_row lines laid as a crown sequence. Needs #156 so the points are fetched. Proof: unit test with a fixture cell holding three tree points and a canopy raster; every point inside the cell yields a crown or a logged rejection. No live-world test. Helps: any cell with surveyed trees, all worlds. REVIEW 2026-10-27: say whether mapped tree points with no lidar canopy peak (young trees) are kept as small crowns or rejected with a logged reason. Unblocked 2026-10-27: #156 done. WAVE2 2026-10-27: claimed by orchestrate-rest.

tasks.title: Ground reads pitch, playground, construction and allotment areas and their surface tag
tasks.notes: Cause: OSMGround._poly reads garden and park (as grass) and wood and scrub, and ignores leisure=pitch, playground, track, landuse=construction, allotments and natural=wetland, grassland, shrubbery; surface=* on polygons is not read either. Deliver: map these tags to a ground kind and priority, choosing the floor from surface and sport where tagged (e.g. tartan, asphalt, grass); keep landuse=residential, retail, commercial, industrial unread (they must not paint under houses). Proof: unit tests in the OSMGround fixture style, one row per tag asserting kind and priority. No live-world test. Helps: any cell with sports pitches, playgrounds or building sites, all worlds. Unblocked 2026-10-27: #156 done.

tasks.title: Building evidence carries roof, height and mapped entrance tags to the designer
tasks.notes: Cause: roof:shape, roof:levels and height are in the cached building clips but only building:levels is read (lidar_heightmap.map_levels); entrance=* points are not fetched, and the facade plan (#145) lists entrances from photos only. Deliver: put roof:shape, roof:levels and height in the feature evidence table as hints beside lidar (never an override); fetch entrance points and offer them as candidate door positions snapped to the footprint edge, ranked main before service and emergency. Proof: evidence-table unit tests with a fixture footprint carrying those tags, and a snap test for an entrance node. No live-world test. Helps: any building with mapped tags, all worlds. Unblocked 2026-10-27: #156 done. WAVE2 2026-10-27: claimed by orchestrate-rest.

tasks.title: Water-body candidates carry the mapped way id and source, and streams are not proposed as ponds
tasks.notes: Split from #156; premise corrected on review. cell_features.missing_water_bodies already feeds OSMGround.water to water_body_components, so nothing needs to be handed over. Real gaps: OSMGround keeps only columns, so a candidate's refs are synthetic water_<x>_<z> and cannot name the mapped way; the candidate provenance source is not set to vector_map (not found where it would be set); stream and drain line columns merge into pond components and are labelled pond. Deliver: polygon water and line water are kept as separate sources in OSMGround; water-body candidates carry the OSM way id and provenance source vector_map; stream lines are not proposed as ponds. Files: lib/sources/ground_sources.py (keep way ids for polygons), lib/builds/water_body.py, lib/journal/cell_features.py, lib/journal/test_cell_features.py. Proof: unit test with a fixture clip holding a natural=water polygon (way 141657072 style id) and a stream line: one candidate with that way id and source vector_map, and no candidate from the stream. No live-world test. Blocked by #162 so culverts do not become ponds; #156 is needed only for the live effect (the pool is fetched), not for the fixture test. Helps: the pond in 48,-45 (I-014), any cell with ponds or fountains. Unblocked 2026-10-27: #162 done. WAVE2 2026-10-27: claimed by orchestrate-rest.

tasks.title: Doors on stepped rotated walls get a built jamb where no framed cell exists
tasks.notes: Split from #143 review; revised on independent review. Cause (2026-10-27 rebuilds): on mass edges rotated ~25-30 degrees the wall steps in 1-2 cell runs. _entrance_wall_candidates already returns the nearest framed cell, so the nearest one can be ~14 blocks from the portal (Jubilee 18-A register 6267,-5523, framed cell only at 6254,-5533) simply because none is nearer; its jamb test is f.walls membership, not solid blocks at b and b+1 (unverified whether this matches guard_door_frames), and its fallback to unframed cells is then refused by the guard (SystemExit with the door-frames json). Deliver: plan_doors / _set_door_leaf build the missing jamb blocks at b+1 and b+2 (and keep them in the plan's keep set) so a door stays on the register cell; the framed-cell test uses block solidity like the guard; any door still moved away from the register coordinate prints its distance. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_door_frames.py. Blocked by #143 (both edit _set_door_leaf and plan_doors). Proof: stepped-wall fixture: door_frame_issues returns [] and the door stays on the register cell (distance 0). No live-world test. Double-leaf landing is #165. Helps: every building not aligned to the grid, all worlds.

tasks.title: Planned double doors land as two leaves on a stepped wall
tasks.notes: Split from #164 review. Cause: on stepped walls the second leaf needs a lateral neighbour cell that is wall at b and b+1; pairing across a step (diagonal-adjacent cell) is refused by the frame guard and would put the two leaves in different planes, so do not do that. Seen 2026-10-27: west 40-A/40-B, susu 42-C, retail 57-A plan double and land single. Deliver: after #164 builds the jamb, plan_doors pairs leaves laterally only and builds the step block at the shared step. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/test_feature_build.py. Proof: stepped-wall fixture: a double entrance gives two leaves in one plane with door_frame_issues empty; a fixture with no lateral room still falls back to one leaf with the 'no pair cell' line. No live-world test. Helps: every building not aligned to the grid, all worlds.
